newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK leadership candidate wants leniency for dissidents.
newsitem.headline: HK leadership candidate wants leniency for dissidents.

text.p: Hong Kong's former chief judge Sir Ti Liang Yang pledged on Saturday to press for a lenient approach to dissidents if he became the territory's first leader after Britain hands it bank to China next year.

"I would say that if I have any influence at all, and the chief executive is bound to have some inlufence...I would prefer a lenient approach rather than a vigorous approach," he told government radio.

The British colony reverts to Beijing's control next July 1 and becomes a Special Administrative Region of China under a leader to be chosen next month by a Beijing-controlled 400-member Selection Committee, and not by universal suffrage.
Yang is one of the declared candidates for the post.

This week, Beijing condemned as illegal the escape of dissident Wang Xizhe from the country to the United States via Hong Kong. Pro-democracy activists in Hong Kong fear China will shut down the escape route after the handover.
China has also charged another dissident Wang Dan of plotting to overthrow the government. He had been held without charge since May 1995.

A group of demonstrators on Saturday protested outside the building of the Xinhua news agency, the de facto Chinese embassy in Hong Kong, to demand Wang's release. Such demonstrations have almost been a daily event this week.
